title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1973-12-02
source: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a mellow, jam‑heavy show with standout second‑set sequences and solid performances despite occasional out‑of‑tune moments.
ai_review.review: The recording (a soundboard source) is praised for its clarity after a modest pitch correction, and the band delivers an especially loose and melodic performance highlighted by extended jams on "Let It Grow," "Playing in the Band," and the Mind Left Body/Truckin' sequence. While the first set is described as slower and a bit uneven, the second‑set flow is lauded for its seamless segues and powerful renditions of "Wharf Rat," "Big River," and a soaring "Morning Dew."

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers give high marks (5 and 4 stars) and focus on strong musical moments; recording is noted as soundboard with good sonic quality, yielding an overall rating in the 4‑star range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Recorded from Dick's #14 (DiP14) with a later pitch correction of -1.5%; reviewers note clear, crisp sound despite occasional out‑of‑tune guitars and minor vocal issues.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is described as slower and uneven with some out‑of‑tune moments; the second set shines with a tight sequence of segues—Wharf Rat > Mississippi > Playing in the Band > Mind Left Body > He's Gone > Truckin'—creating a high‑energy climax that carries through to the encores.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for lyrical depth and beautiful piano/keyboard work; his guitar shines on "Brown‑Eyed Women" and "Big River," though he “floats New Speedway” without fully landing it later.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals are noted as uneven early in the run but strong on "Wharf Rat" and other second‑set numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Piano/keyboard described as beautiful, adding to the mellow vibe of the show.
